glossary.plain: The harm or cost of a breach, computed from the record, assessed by a member, or undetermined.
Something the group asks of someone outside it, with the reply, the clock and the correspondence.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: an act (any button that changes the record)

glossary.plain: A prepared request or complaint text, and a bundle of facts assembled for a lawyer; not legal advice.
Seven stages of pressing a breach, from documenting it to political accountability.
A deadline on an action, always with the law or promise it comes from.
Everything that wants a member, grouped by case: to-dos, things noticed, and signals.

Anything a member does that changes the record: choose it, see what it would refuse, give the reason, get a receipt.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: action (an outward request)

glossary.plain: How heavy an act is: reversible, reasoned, terminal, attested, irreversible.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: the canon 'rung ladder' of steps release → ratify → publish (System Design §3 row 12)

glossary.plain: How an act behaves on many items at once: all or nothing, report what moved, or item by item.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: rung (weight was the ladder's old name)

glossary.plain: A bounded machine session that looks, suggests and asks for captures; it never decides.
Marks anything a machine proposed; it is not evidence until a member acts on it.
A request for the system to fetch a public address later, which the source may refuse.
Material handed over by someone without an account, waiting for a member to decide.
Objective: what a project needs, with a test. Goal: something being pursued. Aspiration: a standing value.
A notice that something your work rests on changed, asking for a second look.
Re-checking a document's public address on a schedule to see if it changed or vanished.
Local rules and deadlines for a place, chosen by an administrator.
A signing key proves who signed; an assistant key lets a machine act; a source login opens a paywalled source.
